key_claims.claim: First-trimester FMF risk strata and specific biomarkers remain independent predictors of breakthrough preterm preeclampsia even among aspirin-treated high-risk women.
Cesarean scar pregnancies continuing beyond 14 weeks carry very high pooled rates of placenta accreta spectrum and hysterectomy, with CSP subtype and myometrial thickness as key risk modifiers.
Graded family history of VTE confers incrementally higher postpartum VTE risk in primiparae, supporting hereditary scoring for thromboprophylaxis decisions.
Advanced machine learning algorithms applied to registry-level variables achieve only modest AUC for term stillbirth prediction, indicating fundamental limits of this approach.
IOTA-based models for adnexal lesion characterization in pregnancy show variable performance across studies, and heterogeneity precludes meta-analysis.
